subject: [RFC PATCH v4 1/3] mm/zswap: release retired pools via queue_rcu_work() instead of synchronize_rcu()

reviews.author: Jianyue Wu
reviews.summary: Reviewer Jianyue Wu noted that hitting the 15-pool cap would be an annoying failure mode, even if it should be rare, and suggested switching to an IDR with IDs in the 1..255 range, keeping 0 as the invalid entry value, and factoring the lookup/allocation path into a zswap_pool_find_or_create() helper.
reviews.raw_body:
Agreed. Hitting the 15-pool cap would be an annoying failure mode, even
if it should be rare.
I will switch this to an IDR with IDs in the 1..255 range, keeping 0 as
the invalid entry value, and factor the lookup/allocation path into a
zswap_pool_find_or_create() helper.

Best regards,
Jianyue

2026-09-02.patch_summary: This patch replaces the dynamic zswap_pools list with a fixed pools array to improve performance and reduce the likelihood of failure modes such as pool corruption or memory leaks. The new approach uses an idr (indirectly referenced) data structure to manage the pools, which allows for more efficient lookups and insertions. A find_or_create function is also introduced to simplify the process of finding or creating a zswap pool.
